ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based CDD/EDD under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 and its AML/CFT Regulations. All shareholders and ultimate beneficial owners at or above the 25% threshold, and any person exercising de facto control, must be screened against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, and any domestic alert or designation issued by the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit. Foreign and domestic PEPs, their family members and close associates are classified as higher-risk and require senior management approval, source of wealth and source of funds verification, and enhanced ongoing monitoring. Screening must be refreshed at least quarterly and upon any trigger event; all positive and negative hits must be documented in the AML file maintained by the licensed registered agent for inspection by MCIL and the FIU.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: MCIL Companies e-Services Portal (Samoa International Companies Registry, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour) at www.mcil.gov.ws
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory register is maintained in English. The proposed legal name must be in Latin/Roman script; Samoan diacritics are accepted. Any non-Latin brand or trade name, including Chinese, must be transliterated into Latin script for the reserved registered name. The company may adopt an additional parallel non-Latin trade name for commercial branding, provided the registered Latin name is used in all statutory filings. Full Chinese-language constitutive documents are permissible as internal governance instruments when accompanied by a certified English translation lodged with the registered agent.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Institute (where implying an educational or professional body)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: An extension of the name reservation may be applied for within the final 7 days of the initial 30-day window and is renewable for further 30-day periods at the Registrar's discretion. If a proposed name is rejected or objected to as prohibited or undesirable, the applicant or its licensed registered agent shall: (1) file a written reconsideration request with the Registrar of International Companies within 14 days of the refusal, attaching availability-search evidence and explaining why the name does not contravene the International Companies Act 1988 (as amended); (2) if reconsideration is refused, lodge an administrative appeal to the Minister of Commerce, Industry and Labour within 30 days; and (3) as a final resort, seek judicial review in the Supreme Court of Samoa, while concurrently filing a fresh name reservation under a modified name to avoid incorporation delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible for the statutory registered office. Every International Company must maintain a physical registered office in Samoa at the premises of its licensed registered agent, customarily in Apia. A virtual office may be used only for correspondence and marketing purposes and cannot satisfy the registered office requirement of the International Companies Act 1988.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for the remote screen-share and IoT software licensing model; estimated below 5% annual probability of an unannounced inspection of the company itself. However, the licensed registered agent is subject to ongoing MCIL supervision and may be inspected with or without notice, and the Registrar retains power to require production of books and records on demand.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), as amended, including the International Companies (Amendment) Act 2008; applicable provisions concerning incorporation, constitution, share capital, registered office, registered agent, directors and secretary.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), in coordination with the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Apia, Samoa.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation of an International Company (Form IC-1), together with the Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum authorised or paid-up capital is prescribed for an International Company. The company may be incorporated with zero paid-up capital; shares may have par or no par value; and no escrow or capital deposit account is required before or after registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Memorandum and Articles of Association filed with the Registrar of International Companies are approved and adopted as the Company's constitution. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the subscription list is accepted, that 100 ordinary shares at par are allotted to the initial subscriber, and that the register of members is opened. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office located at the address named in the Articles is established in Samoa, and that the licensed registered agent shall maintain such office, statutory records and registers. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Director A], [Director B] and [Director C] are appointed as directors, and [Secretary] is appointed as corporate secretary, each to act with full corporate authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Engage Licensed Registered Agent and Reserve Company Name
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SIFA-licensed International Company registered agent; name index maintained by the Registrar of International Companies, MCIL, Apia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Select and retain a registered agent authorised by SIFA. Instruct the agent to conduct a name availability search against the International Companies register and to reserve the proposed corporate name. The name must end in 'Limited', 'Ltd.' or the Samoan equivalent, and must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing Samoan company, government body or prohibited word.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the passport of the beneficial owner and each proposed director
Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement, not older than 3 months)
Declaration of intended business activities (ISIC 6201 remote desktop software)
Proposed company name and corporate suffix
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or queried, submit an alternative name through the same registered agent within 14 days; name reservation may be renewed; no additional state fee applies for one substitute name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare, Execute and Deliver Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered agent; notary public in Samoa or in the jurisdiction of signature
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent drafts the Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association in English. The initial subscriber and first directors execute the documents before a notary public. The registered agent files the executed originals with the Registrar and keeps certified copies for its own statutory file.
required_dossiers: Consent of the registered agent to act
Consent of each director to act
Certified copies of identification of subscribers and directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry requests amendments, the agent may execute a corrective resolution and refile under the same application number; a 30-day curative period is generally available.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Application for Incorporation and Pay State Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, MCIL, Apia; SIFA online or counter filing window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form IC-1 together with the constitution, declaration of compliance and registered agent confirmation. Pay the prescribed government filing fee by wire or SIFA-approved portal. Obtain a stamped application receipt; the Registrar will process the application and issue a Certificate of Incorporation upon approval.
required_dossiers: Registered agent consent and confirmation of office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the application is queried, the registered agent must submit a written response within 10 working days; unresolved queries may be cured by refiling with SIFA or MCIL without prejudice to the original incorporation date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pass First Board Resolutions and Appoint Directors and Officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Initial sole or joint subscriber; first board of directors; registered agent for lodgment of registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting or pass a written unanimous resolution. The board adopts the constitution, establishes the registered office, allots shares, appoints directors and secretary, and authorises the registered agent to maintain registers. File the register of directors and officers with the registered office; the Registry need not be notified unless the Constitution imposes a public filing.
required_dossiers: Written first board resolution (or minutes of first board meeting)
Consent of each director and secretary
Notice of registered office address and registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the resolution is administratively rejected, the board may pass a ratifying resolution; any missing consent is obtained and filed without penalty if cured within 21 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Statutory Registers, Issue Share Certificates and Maintain Company Seal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the register of members, register of directors, register of secretaries and register of charges. Issue share certificates to the subscriber and deliver a copy to the registered agent. If a company seal is adopted, ensure it is kept at the registered office and used only by persons authorised by the board.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any clerical errors in registers by board resolution and annotate the register with the date of correction; no Registry filing is required for private International Companies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Certificate of Incorporation and Post-Incorporation Corporate Kit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies; SIFA corporate services section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Retrieve the Certificate of Incorporation, certified Memorandum and Articles, and certificate of good standing. Confirm the tax-exempt status of the International Company and request an updated SIFA endorsement if needed by obligors or payment processors. This step closes the formation phase; no operational licence is required for remote desktop/IoT software without a physical industrial facility.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a certificate contains a discrepancy, request reissue by statutory declaration under the International Companies Act 1987; SIFA will correct and return the certificate with a revised date only where clearly erroneous.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - no industrial licensing authority is triggered for a non-physical ISIC 6201 remote desktop software business. If any physical office is later opened, the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) and the Samoa Bureau of Standards would be the relevant administrative bodies.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No operating, manufacturing or trade licence is required for remote desktop access and IoT telemetry software delivered digitally under the International Companies Act 1987.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE), Samoa
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no preliminary environmental report or full EIA is required for a software-only service with no land use, construction, factory operations, wastewater, industrial emissions or hazardous waste generation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to the company's core activities. Should an administrative office exist, it must comply with Samoa's general waste disposal requirements and maintain normal sanitary wastewater connections; no VOC or industrial discharge thresholds are triggered.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not required for a remote-screen-share software provider operating with virtual staff and no physical premises. If a brick-and-mortar office is established, the company must obtain a fire safety clearance from the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority, a building occupancy certificate from MCIL or the applicable authority, and pass basic occupational safety inspections under Samoa's labour and employment regulations for any employees present in Samoa.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Samoa Ministry for Revenue – Inland Revenue Division (administered through Samoa Tax Online portal at www.tax.gov.ws)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity with no Samoa permanent establishment is not required to obtain a national TIN for income tax purposes. If a taxable presence or VAGST registration obligation arises, the entity must apply via Samoa Tax Online using Form TIN-01, submitting certified copies of the certificate of incorporation, memorandum and articles, foreign registration certificate, director passports, and a local agent/representative appointment letter. International Companies incorporated under the International Companies Act 1987 are automatically tax-exempt and are not issued a TIN unless they elect conversion to a local company or otherwise become subject to Samoa domestic taxation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Samoa does not provide a check-the-box election under domestic law. An International Company may voluntarily elect to convert to a local company under the Companies Act 2008, thereby abandoning the International Company tax-exempt status and becoming subject to the Income Tax Ordinance 1974 and VAGST Act 2008. Hybrid mismatch elections are not available under Samoa domestic law; however, treaty-based limitation-of-benefits and anti-avoidance rules may apply to prevent artificial use of the exempt IC regime.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 250,000 of taxable supplies made in Samoa in any consecutive 12-month period; registration is mandatory once threshold is met, but voluntary registration is available for businesses below the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Samoa does not currently impose real-time e-invoicing, fiscal clearance, or digital stamping requirements. Registered VAGST suppliers must issue tax invoices containing prescribed particulars: supplier name, VAGST registration number, date, description, quantity, price, tax amount, and total. Electronic invoices are permitted if they preserve the integrity of prescribed particulars; the Samoa Revenue Authority retains the right to audit and require digital access to invoice records.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from Samoa in accordance with the Customs Act attract VAGST zero-rating if physically removed from Samoa within the prescribed period and supported by customs export documentation. Services supplied to a non-resident recipient who is outside Samoa at the time of supply, and are not performed in Samoa or not connected with land or goods in Samoa, are zero-rated for VAGST. The remote screen-share and IoT software services delivered to offshore clients qualify as exported services only where the recipient is outside Samoa, the benefit is enjoyed outside Samoa, and the contract does not create a physical performance nexus in Samoa.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Commissioner may conduct an audit to verify the physical export, final destination, arm’s length price, and receipt of foreign currency. Failure to produce the mandatory customs documentation, failure to repatriate foreign exchange within 180 days, or claiming zero-rating on supplies that are not genuinely exported triggers a full VAGST clawback at 15%, plus a late payment penalty of 10% of the unpaid tax and interest of 2% per month or part thereof. Deliberate evasion or fraudulent zero-rating claims are subject to civil penalties of up to 150% of the tax shortfall, criminal fines not exceeding WST 100,000, and imprisonment for up to 10 years, together with permanent loss of zero-rating privileges.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS; Faletupe Tutotonu o Samoa), established under the Central Bank Act 1984 and responsible for administering the Exchange Control Act 1976, the Financial Institutions Act 2012, and Samoa's AML/CFT licensing framework for authorised dealer banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoa tala (WST) is a domestically settled currency with no active offshore interbank market; current-account payments for genuine trade in services are permitted through authorised dealer banks, while capital-account transactions require CBS exchange-control approval or an authorised dealer's standing power. The Samoa International Company (IC) is structured as non-resident and is tax-exempt, but deposits that enter the licensed Samoan banking system become subject to CBS surveillance, reporting thresholds, and exchange-control documentation. Profit remittance and dividend distributions are executable after evidence of substance, audited or reviewed management accounts, tax status confirmation, and a completed CBS exchange-control application or authorised dealer declaration; convertibility of WST outside Samoa remains limited and is normally achieved by USD or AUD settlement through the offshore treasury network of a licensed bank.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Samoa's Exchange Control Act 1976 and the CBS Exchange Control Manual, exporters of goods and services must repatriate export proceeds no later than 180 days after the date of export or service performance; proceeds received in a foreign currency must be offered for sale to an authorised dealer and, unless CBS relief is obtained, 100% of the receipt must be converted into Samoa tala within the statutory time frame. For a remote-screen-share and IoT telemetry software IC, digital service subscriptions collected by global payment processors (Stripe/Paddle) are not treated as surrenderable funds while settled offshore; only such proceeds remitted into a licensed Samoan bank account enter the surrender net. Where an IC holds a CBS-approved foreign-currency account, conversion relief may permit retention in USD/AUD for matching future vendor payments, but every export invoice, payment gateway settlement report, and bank credit advice must be retained as the evidentiary chain for the mandatory repatriation calculation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Samoan Tala Operational Account, USD Foreign-Currency Account, and non-resident Corporate Escrow Account
Operational Account in WST and USD, and Capital Raising Sub-Account
WST Operational Account and USD Nostro Settlement Account
Domestic Operational Account and Foreign-Currency Savings/Current Facility

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low-to-Medium. Samoa does not issue a standalone electronic-money-institution (EMI) licence to non-resident fintechs, and deposit-taking activity requires a banking licence under the Financial Institutions Act 2012. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise, Payoneer, or neobanks are not adequate substitutes for a Samoan licensed bank when the IC requires WST clearing, CBS-compliant invoicing, or letters of comfort for treasury due diligence. The legally preferred architecture is a split-rail model: a regulated Samoan commercial bank for equity, statutory filings, and B2B treasury flows, plus a recognised global PSP (Stripe/Paddle) for merchant collection of low-risk SaaS subscriptions; the PSP settlement must be swept under a defined liquidity policy rather than treated as a bank facility.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Samoan law does not impose a universal requirement that every director appear physically in Apia, but each bank's AML/CFT programme requires at least one executive director, the ultimate beneficial owner, and the designated authorised signatory to complete an enhanced-interview process via live video conference or in-person meeting. In practice, banks with a High onboarding tier accept reliable e-verification and apostilled corporate documents; however, a physical bank visit or a professional introducer meeting in Apia materially accelerates facility approval for a non-resident IC whose activity is digital cross-border services.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident International Company with nominee director conventions, bearer instruments, or an opaque beneficial-ownership chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Incorporation, current Memorandum and Articles of Association, register of directors and shareholders, register of charges, updated beneficial-ownership register, passport pages for all directors and ultimate beneficiaries, independent corporate registry search, and a written explanation of any nominee arrangement including the underlying trust or corporate services agreement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-exempt offshore status combined with no physically occupied office and no identifiable staff in Samoa.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Samoa International Company good-standing certificate from the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour, substance memorandum describing the remote-service operating model, global headcount and contractor list, office or virtual-office lease, audited or reviewed financial statements, treasury and user-support service agreements, and a detailed customer flow covering remote desktop access and IoT telemetry deployment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Heavy reliance on Stripe/Paddle merchant settlement without a traditional bank-account relationship, causing opacity in source-of-funds verification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Platform KYB/KYC approval certificates, merchant legal-name attestation, 12-month settlement statements, clearing reports by payment method and country, chargeback and refund ledger, customer invoices and end-user contracts, PCI DSS compliance evidence, and a board-minute policy mapping merchant settlement to the authorised-dealer bank account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP, negative-media, or high-risk jurisdictional flags raised against a shareholder, director, or payment corridor.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: World-Check or equivalent sanctions/PEP/negative-news screening report, passport and tax-residence certificate, bank reference from the shareholder's home institution, sworn-source-of-wealth statement, independent credit enquiry, and signed undertakings that no proceeds derive from restricted jurisdictions or unlawful activity.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inward equity capital to the Samoa IC must be routed by SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's regulated banking institution to the IC's authorised-dealer bank account in Samoa, using the beneficiary bank's BIC, the IC legal name as account holder, and an International Transactions purpose code that maps to IMF BPM6 'Equity Capital' or Samoa CBS Form ECA-1 'Inward Direct Investment'. The authorised dealer will require a board resolution approving the share subscription, a subscription letter or share allotment certificate, source-of-funds evidence, and confirmation that the Samoa IC has no minimum paid-up capital requirement. The transaction must not be split into trade-payment codes such as 'Computer Services Software' merely to bypass exchange-control review; if the funds are share capital, the bank's accounting entry and the IC's statutory register of members must both record equity. Upon receipt, the treasury function should match the SWIFT Unique End-to-End Transaction Reference, the bank advice, and the Central Bank of Samoa Form ECA-1 stamp to preserve a complete audit trail.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for operational trade in the remote-support and IoT context should be cleared through SWIFT MT103 for vendor invoices, software licence royalties, data-centre hosting fees, and independent contractor remuneration, with each payment referencing the underlying service contract and the prescribed Samoa balance-of-payments service code. For physical hardware procurement (IoT edge devices, secure gateways, or development kits supplied by overseas manufacturers), the appropriate clearing rail is a commercial letter of credit issued by the Samoan authorised dealer by SWIFT MT700, with settlement effected by MT103 or MT202 under the LC terms; Standby Letters of Credit (MT760) may be used for vendor performance guarantees or contractual security. All outbound wires must quote the CBS Exchange Control application reference or the authorised dealer's standing approval where applicable, and the treasury policy should maintain a weekly reconciliation of SWIFT payments against approved tax-compliant invoices and subscription revenue recognised in the books of the Samoa IC.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable outright forward contracts between WST and USD executed with a CBS-licensed authorised dealer bank, permitted solely to hedge firm projected software licensing receipts or known Samoan tala expenses.

Cross-currency swaps between WST and USD involving a licensed commercial bank in Samoa, subject to board approval, CBS exchange-control reporting, and documented economic exposure arising from the remote-screen-share and IoT subscription business.
Overnight foreign-exchange swaps used for treasury liquidity management by the authorised dealer to convert temporary WST surplus into USD without creating speculative open positions.

Offshore non-deliverable forwards on WST permitted only as a risk-management overlay for a defined invoicing mismatch, provided the instrument has no speculative leverage and the hedging committee maintains full documentation of the underlying receivables.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of WST 20 per day up to WST 500; continued default may lead to administrative strike-off after 12 months

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered Agent (to be filed with Registrar of International Companies on request)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 14 days after any shareholding transfer; annual confirmation due on incorporation anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance is an offence under Anti-Money Laundering Act; fines up to WST 50,000 and director disqualification

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory independent audit for Samoa International Companies; audit only required if appointed by shareholders or if the company engages in financial services licensed under the International Financial Services Act
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) if voluntary audit prepared; otherwise internal accounts permitted under simple cash basis or any reasonable accounting system

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The registered agent must maintain a current UBO register; any shareholding transfer requiring an entry must be recorded and confirmed annually on the incorporation anniversary, disclosing all individuals holding 10% or more direct or indirect interest.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% standard Samoa corporate income tax rate for resident and non-resident companies; effective 0% for an International Company (IC) under the International Companies Act 1987, which grants a 20-year income tax exemption renewable for a further 20 years.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IC exemption from income tax, capital gains tax, stamp duty, estate duty and gift duty; the exemption extends to shareholders, directors, officers and employees; the only recurring statutory charge is the annual government fee of US$100 to US$500 depending on registered capital.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: SIFA Annual Return for International Companies (Form AR-IC), lodged electronically by the licensed Samoa registered agent through the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) online registry portal; no income tax return is required because the IC is exempt from Samoa income tax.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within 30 days after each anniversary of the date of incorporation; the annual government fee is payable at the same time.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full legal name of the International Company as set out in the Certificate of Incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact registered name without abbreviations or translations; any change of name requires prior approval of the Registrar.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Unique IC registration number issued by the Registrar.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Copy directly from the Certificate of Incorporation; errors delay processing and may trigger late fees.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Physical street address of the IC's registered office in Samoa.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must be a physical Samoan address maintained by the registered agent; a P.O. Box alone is not acceptable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name and SIFA licence number of the Samoan registered agent or licensed law firm.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The agent must be licensed under the International Companies Act 1987; non-residents cannot act as registered agent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full names, residential addresses, nationalities, and government-issued identification numbers of all directors.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident directors are permitted; a Samoa-resident alternate director or registered agent nominee is commonly used and must be disclosed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Names and addresses of all shareholders, classes and numbers of shares held, and a declaration identifying the ultimate beneficial owner.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents may hold 100% of the shares; beneficial ownership information is collected for AML/CFT purposes and is not publicly accessible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Authorised capital, issued share capital, par value and form of consideration paid.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No minimum capital requirement applies; shares may be denominated in any major currency and fully paid-up.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Particulars of any mortgage, charge or lien over the IC's assets registered with the Registrar.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If none, state 'None'; cross-border financing charges must be recorded to be enforceable against third parties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Signed declaration by a director and the registered agent confirming the correctness of the return and compliance with all statutory requirements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The declaration must be signed by a natural person; false declarations trigger director liability and criminal penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing fee of 10% of the annual government fee for each month or part of a month of default, up to a maximum of 100% of the fee; three consecutive years of non-filing leads to compulsory strike-off and dissolution, with restoration requiring significant additional fees and reopening the company to third-party claims.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for dividends paid by an IC to non-resident shareholders under the International Companies Act 1987 exemption; the standard Samoa statutory withholding tax rate for dividends from other companies is 15%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Samoa's DTA network covers Australia, New Zealand, Fiji and Norway. Protocol: (1) obtain a Samoa Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the Ministry for Revenue if the company is treaty-resident in Samoa; (2) submit the relevant treaty relief claim form and TRC to the payer before payment; (3) the payer applies the treaty withholding rate instead of the statutory 15%; (4) retain the TRC, treaty declaration and ownership documentation for at least 5 years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: 0% for interest and royalties paid out of an IC; the standard Samoa statutory withholding rates are 15% on interest and 15% on royalties paid to non-residents, potentially reduced under the Australia, New Zealand, Fiji or Norway DTAs.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory Local File or Master File threshold is prescribed in Samoa; ICs are exempt from income tax and therefore outside the transfer pricing documentation regime. For any residual scope involving a Samoa-resident related entity, the arm's length principle under the Income Tax Act 1974 applies, and contemporaneous documentation is recommended where cross-border related-party software revenue exceeds an annual equivalent of USD 1,000,000 (approximately WST 2,700,000).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Applicable. Samoa's economic substance regime, administered by SIFA, requires an IC carrying on relevant activities (including software and remote services, distribution and service centre operations, financing and leasing, or intellectual property holding) to demonstrate that core income-generating activities are directed and managed in Samoa with adequate premises, employees, expenditure and board governance; alternatively, the IC must prove tax residence in a qualifying foreign jurisdiction. A substance declaration is filed annually with Form AR-IC, and non-compliance triggers penalties, information exchange with treaty partners, and possible strike-off.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the IC as a booking shell: global remote-screen-share and telemetry subscription revenue is invoiced through Samoa solely to avoid foreign and Samoan taxation, while management, customers, developers and servers remain entirely outside Samoa and no economic activity occurs there.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Compensating assessments and penalties of 100% to 200% of tax evaded under the Income Tax Act 1974; strike-off and dissolution of the IC; disclosure of the structure to foreign tax authorities under Samoa's tax information exchange agreements and DTAs.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and shadow directors are jointly and severally liable for evaded amounts; criminal conviction carries imprisonment up to 7 years, civil restitution, asset freezing and travel bans.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Absence of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Nominee or bare companies with non-resident directors exercising no real control, letterbox registered office, failure to file the annual substance declaration, and no records of board meetings or strategic decisions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of up to WST 50,000 under the International Companies Act 1987 and SIFA regulations, compulsory strike-off, loss of the IC tax exemption, and automatic exchange of beneficial ownership information with foreign regulators.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Disqualification from acting as director, personal fines for false substance declarations, travel restrictions, and imprisonment up to 5 years for knowingly making or permitting a false filing.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure of the registered agent, directors and beneficial owners to identify and disclose true ownership; accepting payments for remote-access and telemetry tools through Stripe or Paddle without proper onboarding and sanctions screening; or processing proceeds of cybercrime and ransomware through the IC's merchant accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to WST 100,000 per breach under Samoa's Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 (as amended); suspension or revocation of the registered agent's licence; freezing and confiscation orders over the IC's assets and merchant accounts; mandatory reporting to the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face criminal liability of up to 5 years' imprisonment for materially false KYC or beneficial-ownership declarations and personal civil restitution for moneys laundered through the IC.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlicensed Payment/Financial Service and Sanctions Exposure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the IC as an unlicensed money transmitter, holding customer deposits, operating an electronic wallet, or processing payments outside Stripe/Paddle's licensed merchant model; alternatively, selling the remote-support software to sanctioned customers in jurisdictions prohibited by UN, EU or US sanctions regimes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to WST 250,000 and confiscation of assets for unregulated financial activity under Samoa's financial services legislation; merchant account termination, Stripe/Paddle blacklisting, designation on international sanctions lists, and consequential global asset freezes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal fines, extradition exposure, imprisonment up to 10 years under Samoa's financial crimes provisions and applicable foreign sanctions legislation; directors may be subject to international travel bans and personal supervision orders.
